rationale: Used widely: SSE streams in crates/engine/src/http/order_events.rs and admin.rs, crates/monokulo/src/live.rs and logs_page.rs (stream::unfold/select/StreamExt), join_all in proof/mod.rs, proof/anchor.rs and live-settings registry.rs, and future::select/Either in engine run.rs and daemon_fallback.rs. axum, reqwest and hyper-util depend on it anyway, so dropping the direct edges saves nothing.

alternative: keep; if wallet-cli size matters later, swap to rustyline (not in workspace) and accept losing the IDE-style completion menu with right-hand descriptions and OSC133 mouse clicks
size_impact: dropping it outright: -330 KiB .text in wallet-cli, -17 exclusive crates / ~151k src lines from build (crossterm, chrono, strum, derive_more, signal-hook...). A rustyline swap would win back only part of that; a hand-rolled raw-mode editor would win most of it
maintainability: Owning a line editor means raw-mode termios, ANSI rendering, wide-char/grapheme cursor maths, history file locking and terminal quirks across emulators: lots of platform edge cases for a dev/operator CLI. Not security-sensitive, but a big test burden
rationale: It is used fully, not lightly: crates/cli-wallet/src/bin/cli/editor.rs:21-25 pulls in Reedline, Emacs keybindings, FileBackedHistory, a custom Completer (:378), a history-prefix Hinter (:480), a syntax Highlighter (:538), a Prompt (:570), an IdeMenu with descriptions (:693) and OSC133 mouse clicks (:717). main.rs:312-322 drives the Signal loop. Only wallet-cli ships it, and that binary is a dev/stagenet wallet, not the payment path. So the 340 KiB costs little. Revisit only if wallet-cli's size or build time starts to matter; rustyline is the cheapest swap.

alternative: none viable workspace-wide: the traits are used as dyn objects. Native async fn in traits is not dyn-compatible, so going without it means hand-written Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + '_>> signatures on every trait and impl
size_impact: ~0: catalog shows 0 exclusive crates and no binary_size rows. It is a proc-macro and stays in the graph through reqwest-middleware, hickory-net and zeromq
maintainability: Hand-boxed futures would be noisy, error-prone boilerplate across ~60 impls (most of them test doubles). async-trait itself is stable and widely used
rationale: KeyCustody (crates/key-custody/src/custody.rs:239), MoneroDaemonClient (crates/engine/src/daemon.rs:271), SettingsStore (crates/live-settings/src/store.rs:25), EvidenceSource (crates/key-custody/src/snp.rs:117) and Reloadable (crates/live-settings/src/section.rs:173) are all held as dyn objects (engine-test-support/src/lib.rs, engine tests, e2e-harness), so native async-fn-in-trait does not work for them. crates/shared/src/http_cache.rs:119,236 implement reqwest-middleware's external Middleware trait, which is itself defined with async_trait. Dropping it would save no binary size or graph weight.

alternative: none viable: it is the token type that syn and quote work on in ui-macros
size_impact: ~0: catalog shows 0 exclusive crates and no binary_size rows. It is compile-time only and is pulled in by every derive in the graph (serde_derive, tokio-macros, thiserror-impl, clap_derive, maud_macros...)
maintainability: None to own; it is a compile-time-only foundation crate
rationale: crates/ui-macros/src/lib.rs (1885 lines) implements the component! macro that is the Rust UI source of truth. It uses proc-macro2 TokenStream/Span/Ident throughout (83 symbol refs). proc_macro's built-in types cannot be used outside the macro context or in unit tests, so swapping to std is not realistic. It is in the build graph through dozens of other proc-macros regardless.

alternative: keep; drop only engine's unused declaration (crates/engine/Cargo.toml:67), and the unused `derive` feature from cli-wallet, engine and wallet-setup
size_impact: ~0: catalog shows 0 exclusive crates and no binary_size rows. It stays in the graph through curve25519-dalek, rustls, aws-lc-rs, hpke, rsa, monero-* and others
maintainability: Volatile-write plus compiler-fence semantics are subtle and security-relevant (the optimiser can elide naive memset clears). Do not hand-roll
rationale: Secret handling across the workspace relies on it. Examples are Zeroizing key material in crates/key-custody/src/snp.rs:152,295,411, crates/key-custody-cli/src/main.rs:90-110, crates/snp-attest/src/guest.rs:73,233, crates/cli-wallet/src/wallet.rs:45-46 and crates/wallet-setup/src/lib.rs:71-115. Manual Drop clears are in crates/monokulo/src/crypto.rs:60 and crates/live-settings/src/value.rs:232. ZeroizeOnDrop derive is used only in crates/key-custody/src/custody.rs:42. The engine declares zeroize but never uses it, so remove that edge as hygiene; it saves nothing.

alternative: keep: it is a dev-dependency only
size_impact: 0 in shipped binaries; it affects test build time only
maintainability: A home-grown generator and shrinker would lose shrinking and regression-file replay, and would be a large test-infra burden
rationale: There are 69 proptest! blocks across 24 engine verification files (e.g. crates/engine/tests/verification/work/money/properties.rs, work/nodes/properties.rs, proof/node_properties.rs) and in key-custody's cfg(test) modules (crates/key-custody/src/plain_properties.rs, router_properties.rs, property_support.rs:13 for the shared Config). It carries the property-based coverage of money, node-fallback and custody logic, and it ships nothing.

alternative: none viable: it builds the output TokenStreams in ui-macros
size_impact: ~0: compile-time only, and pulled in by every derive in the graph (serde_derive, tokio-macros, thiserror-impl...)
maintainability: None to own
rationale: crates/ui-macros/src/lib.rs uses quote! for all of the component! macro's codegen (98 symbol refs). Building TokenStreams by hand with proc_macro2 would roughly double that file and save nothing, because quote stays in the graph through other proc-macros.

alternative: none viable for ui-macros; xtask's use (a syn::visit pass to find tests and their ignore reasons) could become a regex scan, but that would be more fragile
size_impact: ~0: catalog shows 0 exclusive crates and no binary_size rows. It is compile-time and dev tooling only, and already in the graph through serde_derive, async-trait, tokio-macros and others (with `full` enabled)
maintainability: None to own
rationale: crates/ui-macros/src/lib.rs parses the component! DSL with syn (55 symbol refs). xtask/src/summary.rs:8,69-116 uses syn::parse_file and Visit to list tests and read #[ignore = "..."] reasons, which is an exact AST job. syn compiles anyway for the workspace's other proc-macros, so dropping these edges gains nothing.

alternative: none viable: it does consensus-critical transaction construction, scanning and signing
size_impact: -229 KiB .text in wallet-cli only, -2 exclusive crates / ~10k src lines (monero-oxide and the rest stay through monero-daemon-rpc)
maintainability: Re-implementing CLSAG, Bulletproofs+, decoy selection and output scanning is consensus- and privacy-critical cryptography. Never hand-roll it
rationale: crates/cli-wallet/src/lib.rs:73 and crates/cli-wallet/src/wallet.rs:8 use it for ViewPair/address derivation, scanning, and building and signing transactions (124 symbol refs across lib.rs, wallet.rs, faucet.rs and bin/cli/commands.rs). Its weight lands only in wallet-cli. Replacing it would mean writing Monero signing code, which the brief rules out.

alternative: none viable: the only real replacement is hyper-util's client + hyper-rustls, which is reqwest's own stack minus the convenience layer, and reqwest-middleware's http_cache in shared needs reqwest anyway
size_impact: ~0 alone: catalog shows 0 exclusive crates and no binary_size rows, because reqwest-middleware (monokulo, shared) also pulls it in. Treated as a pair, reqwest-middleware's own weight is 1 crate / ~1k src lines / ~10 KiB .text in monokulo. The catalog has no combined figure for the pair, but most of the pair's weight would be rustls + aws-lc-rs, and that TLS stack must stay because remote monerod, webhooks, KDS, OTLP and exchange-rate fetches go over HTTPS. The aws-lc-sys C code is not attributed by cargo-bloat
maintainability: Owning an HTTP client means redirects, timeouts, proxy/Tor (socks), body limits, cookie and form handling for mock-woocommerce, and TLS config: security-sensitive and spec-heavy
rationale: Used in 10 crates. Main sites: crates/monokulo/src/engine_client.rs and webhooks/delivery.rs, crates/shared/src/http_cache.rs (reqwest-middleware cache), crates/shared/src/exchange_rate.rs, crates/engine/src/daemon_rpc.rs, crates/snp-attest/src/kds.rs, crates/telemetry/src/otlp.rs, crates/key-custody-cli (blocking) and crates/cli-wallet. TLS must not be hand-rolled, and the size cost is the TLS provider rather than reqwest. One option to revisit separately: check whether an aws-lc-rs to ring provider swap is wanted (it is a build/C-toolchain question, not a reqwest one).

alternative: std::sync::{Mutex, RwLock} plus a small poisoning-free wrapper is possible for most sites, but engine and shared use try_lock_for(INLINE_LOCK_WAIT) timed locking, which std lacks
size_impact: ~0: catalog shows 0 exclusive crates and no binary_size rows. It is still pulled in by tokio (the `full` feature enables tokio/parking_lot), moka, hickory-resolver, zeromq and crossterm
maintainability: A std wrapper has to handle poisoning (or ignore it) at ~135 call sites, and needs a hand-built timed-lock (spin/sleep or Condvar) for the store lock. That is concurrency code to own, with no size win
rationale: There are ~135 uses of parking_lot::Mutex/RwLock across engine, monokulo, shared, live-settings, telemetry, key-custody and the test crates. crates/engine/src/store/db.rs:254-255 and crates/shared/src/sqlite.rs:226 rely on try_lock_for with a timeout, which std::sync::Mutex does not offer. Guards are returned by type at crates/engine/src/store/mod.rs:326, crates/monokulo/src/db.rs:480 and crates/monokulo/src/http/status_page.rs:89. The crate stays in the graph through tokio and others, so dropping the direct edges would cost churn and gain nothing.

alternative: none worth doing: an own 20-line encode/decode, or consolidating on data-encoding (HEXLOWER, already in the graph), would remove the direct edges only
size_impact: ~0: hex 0.4.3 stays in the graph through monero 0.22, monero-wallet, monero-interface and monero-daemon-rpc (cargo tree -i hex). Only 367-506 bytes .text per binary anyway; 686 src lines.
maintainability: Owning it is trivial, but rewriting about 280 hex::encode and hex::decode call sites in 13 crates is churn with no build or size win. Decoding key and txid material needs exact error behaviour, so a rewrite would also need fresh tests.
rationale: The only API used anywhere is hex::encode (188 sites) and hex::decode (90 sites), in engine, key-custody, cli-wallet, monokulo, xtask and others. The Monero crates the workspace needs depend on hex themselves, so dropping our declarations would not remove the crate or any bytes. Revisit only if monero 0.22 is ever replaced.

alternative: none viable (log, already in the graph, has no spans and no subscriber/OpenTelemetry integration that telemetry relies on)
size_impact: ~0: tracing is pulled in by axum, axum-core, axum-extra, tower, hyper-util, hickory-*, tracing-subscriber and tracing-opentelemetry. Measured exclusive .text is 9.9 KiB in monokulo and 32 KiB in monokulo-engine, and it would not go away.
maintainability: Ecosystem standard, stable 0.1 API. The telemetry crate builds its layers, throttle and client-log plumbing on it.
rationale: There are about 370 path refs to tracing macros and spans across engine (27 files), monokulo (38 files), telemetry (9 files, the subscriber and layer side) and shared. The HTTP stack emits tracing events regardless, so the crate stays in the build whatever we do. Replacing it would mean rewriting telemetry's span-based design for no size gain.

alternative: none viable; sqlx would be heavier and async, and hand-written FFI over libsqlite3-sys would mean owning unsafe code
size_impact: If dropped: -168 KiB .text in monokulo, -163 KiB in monokulo-engine and -142 KiB in wallet-cli (Rust side only; cargo-bloat does not attribute the bundled C SQLite in libsqlite3-sys, the much larger part). Also -6 crates and 32k src lines. No replacement is smaller.
maintainability: SQLite is the store of record for a production instance (payments, settings, logs). Owning unsafe bindings would be security sensitive. Keeping bundled pins the SQLite version, which helps.
rationale: Six crates use it as their database layer: engine (18 files including migrations, with the serialize feature), monokulo (functions and hooks features), shared, telemetry, cli-wallet and xtask. It is the thinnest safe SQLite wrapper there is. The only possible tidy-up is checking whether each feature (serialize, hooks, functions, serde_json) is still needed; dropping one is a small win, not a dependency drop.

alternative: none viable
size_impact: ~0: required by axum, reqwest, serde_json, rusqlite (serde_json feature) and many others. Measured exclusive .text is 5 KiB in monokulo.
maintainability: Foundation crate, stable API. Derives across settings, the HTTP API and the config file.
rationale: Every crate in the workspace derives Serialize and Deserialize: monokulo (38 files), engine (11), shared (10), xtask (10), live-settings, the TOML options registry and the JSON APIs. axum's Json, Form and Query extractors and reqwest require it, so it cannot leave the graph.

alternative: consolidate on the monero-oxide family (monero-wallet, monero-interface and monero-daemon-rpc are already used by cli-wallet), or keep monero-rs
size_impact: If fully replaced: -93 KiB .text in monokulo, -102 KiB in monokulo-engine and -6 exclusive crates (19k src lines). However, monero-oxide crates would then be added to the engine and monokulo builds, so the net is likely about 0 or worse.
maintainability: This is consensus-critical: transaction and block deserialisation, one-time-key and subaddress derivation, and view-key output scanning. It must never be hand-rolled. A migration would touch scanner, daemon_rpc and key-custody outputs and need full re-verification against the replay fixtures.
rationale: The engine decodes every daemon blob into monero::Transaction and monero::Block (crates/engine/src/daemon_rpc.rs:27-29, crates/engine/src/scanner.rs:13-14). key-custody scans outputs with ViewPair, KeyGenerator and SubKeyChecker (crates/key-custody/src/outputs.rs:22-25). monokulo and shared mostly use monero::Network and Address parsing. The workspace now runs two Monero crate families: crates/engine/Cargo.toml:36-43 notes monero-epee comes from monero-oxide while everything else stays in monero-rs types. Converging on one family is worth revisiting when monero-oxide is fully published. Writing our own is not an option.

alternative: none viable
size_impact: ~0: pulled in by axum (json feature), reqwest, rusqlite, cookie_store and monero-daemon-rpc. Measured .text is 157 KiB in monokulo, 108 KiB in monokulo-engine and 31 KiB in key-custody-cli, but it stays.
maintainability: Handles JSON parsing of untrusted input (daemon RPC, plugin and webhook bodies). Should not be hand-rolled.
rationale: Used in 13 crates: daemon RPC bodies in engine (30 files), the admin and merchant APIs in monokulo (40 files), Json<T> settings in live-settings, xtask's generators and ui's component metadata. The HTTP stack depends on it anyway, so there is nothing to remove.

alternative: none viable; possible feature trimming only (several crates declare 'full')
size_impact: ~0 from dropping: axum, hyper, reqwest and hickory all require tokio. Measured .text is 389 KiB in monokulo, 326 KiB in monokulo-engine, 138 KiB in wallet-cli and 77 KiB in key-custody-cli. Narrowing 'full' to the features actually used (engine, monokulo, shared, mock-woocommerce) could shave a little, but the main features stay.
maintainability: The core async runtime for every server. Mature and security-maintained.
rationale: There are over 1,800 path refs: tasks, timers, channels, net and signal handling throughout engine (58 files), monokulo (43 files), shared and key-custody. The whole axum and reqwest stack runs on it. key-custody-cli's 77 KiB comes through key-custody's optional rt/sync/time use, which is legitimate.

alternative: none worth it: askama or minijinja would be a lateral move, and an own html! macro would duplicate maud
size_impact: Small: 5.1 KiB .text in monokulo, 3 exclusive crates and 2.7k src lines. Any replacement templating crate costs about the same.
maintainability: Compile-time-escaped HTML. Owning a templating macro would bring XSS-escaping risk.
rationale: It is the server-rendering layer for all of monokulo's pages (31 files, about 2,000 html! symbol refs). It is also the target of the ui crate's component! macro (crates/ui/src/lib.rs:39 re-exports maud; Component: maud::Render at crates/ui/src/lib.rs:148), which the project treats as its UI source of truth. xtask uses it to generate the stylebook. It is cheap, and replacing it would rewrite every page.

alternative: none viable (raw hyper plus our own router and extractors would be thousands of lines)
size_impact: If dropped: -107 KiB .text in monokulo, -72 KiB in monokulo-engine, and -4 exclusive crates (axum, axum-macros, matchit, serde_path_to_error; 28k src lines). Any replacement router or extractor code would claw most of that back.
maintainability: Owning HTTP routing, extractors and form and query parsing on the public, internet-facing front end would be security sensitive.
rationale: It is the HTTP framework of both servers: monokulo (50 files, about 2,100 symbol refs to Router, extractors, State and middleware) and the engine's admin API and status page (19 files), plus the test harnesses and telemetry's matched-path layer. axum-extra and tower build on it. It is the thinnest mainstream option over hyper.
